segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Well, let's talk about those efforts at communication, the secret covert efforts that have been going on inside the defense national security structure. You write in your Forbidden Science diaries, in October 2021, for the first time you mention someone called Gilbert. It's a pseudonym, but essentially it's a long-lost friend, a discreet master remote viewer at the level of Uri Geller 🤥 and Ingo Swann. And Gilbert tells you that, through official channels, presumably government channels, he was taken to participate in a controlled personal exchange with a supposed alien. And you acknowledge in your diary that these revelations are explosive. And by September 2023 you've received five closely typed pages detailing how Gilbert says he was taken to a US laboratory sheltered inside rock, where military guides exposed him to what they explicitly told him was a living alien entity. Now, do you believe Gilbert's account, Jacques? I know at one stage you query whether this was a fully veridical account. Do you think Gilbert was telling you the truth?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I believe it for two reasons. You know, "believe" is a bad word, it's a religious word, it's a commitment and so on, and everybody is free to believe whatever we want to believe. In science, belief is a contingency. You face a phenomenon, you build a theory of a phenomenon — but there is no such thing as a theory without a way of testing it. Now, I have no way of testing what Gilbert has told me. I'm not going to reveal the rest of his data, because that's his data, and I know there are plans to publish it in the proper way so that everybody has access to it. I have the data, but it's not up to me to publish it. There have been other cases, and I've had one personal occasion of coming face to face with an entity that is very similar to the entity that he describes — but, to my shame, I was so scared, because this was unprepared, I was not intending to do that…

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: So are you saying that you had your own personal encounter with an entity? When did that happen?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yes. I had no communication with that entity, because I was simply too scared, and I mention it in the book. Now, in his case this was very structured. He was asked to be there, and by the way it's not classified — I asked him if it was classified, he said no. And this was 20 years ago, this is not recent.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: So let's go through some of the detail of what you do reveal in Forbidden Science 7. In December 2024 you write that you've seen Gilbert's structured results, and he says he was apparently instructed to put specific questions directly to the entity. And it gets fascinating: some of the questions generated impressions and responses he couldn't decipher. And what you conclude is that there may be two different levels of NHI. Your interpretation, or your friend's interpretation of what he got from the being, is that the higher-level controllers are genuinely alien, whereas the small beings, perhaps the grays associated with UFO encounters, may be primitive biological hybrids specifically engineered for terrestrial operation. Is that your conclusion, Jacques?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Well, again, I'm an information scientist. I try to look for patterns of things, so I don't look at one case separate from others. I look for patterns of cases: in Trinity, in Socorro, in Valensole, and now in the case in Brazil that was revealed recently, Varginha, where we have a dozen entities. These entities were small, they were the size of a 10- or 12-year-old kid. They had two eyes and a mouth, they were breathing air. They did not look like our astronauts with all kinds of suits, support systems. They were breathing air. You could understand any sense from their eyes, and overall their structure was human.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Over the years there have been efforts to theorize in biology about what it would take to create a different kind of human adapted to certain things. We are going to face that problem in space, so NASA has looked at that. But before NASA, certainly in World War II, that question was raised already, and I mention a case from an American biologist who came back from Russia with at least a rumor that the Russians were developing short humanoids for future space missions, because that would save the most expensive part in the space missions we have now, like the Moon: the human pilot. If we could do away with the human pilot, or if we could minimize that pilot, then the technology would be safer and would probably function better. So that question had been discussed in biology. Now, the threshold was a moral threshold: are we permitted to create? I mean, we are clearly at a position where — as you know, the question arose in China recently — was there an experiment to manipulate an egg and create them? So those are very current questions in biology. Could some of the beings be just operators? Because in Brazil especially, they did not seem to be in control at all. And the same thing in Trinity — Trinity is a very important case.
